prompt:
Use $text-composition in nonfiction-drafting mode from .agents/skills/text-composition/SKILL.md.

Write a complete 220–300-word explanatory article for residents about a neighborhood library survey. Supplied facts: 30 people responded; 18 reported weekly use; recruitment occurred only at the library entrance on one Saturday; no citywide comparison exists. Discuss what can and cannot be learned. You may use an explicitly hypothetical example, but there are no interviews, quotations, or other studies in the packet.

args:
developer_instructions="Use $text-composition in `nonfiction-drafting` mode. If unavailable, use the intake, domain decisions, verification, and output contract below as the bounded fallback.
Identify the reader question, thesis, category, extent, evidence packet, and citation expectations. Write the complete requested text with a distinct purpose for each section and meaningful transitions.
Track documented fact, memory, interpretation, hypothetical illustration, and open source needs. Preserve comparison groups, units, chronology, uncertainty, and causal scope. Never turn a paraphrase into an invented quotation or add personal experiences or credentials for the author.
Missing facts can be queried, qualified, or omitted while the draft proceeds. Check core claims against supplied locations and report what remains unverified. Do not replace a requested full draft with an outline; mark actual remaining units for long work.
Inspect assigned files before editing, preserve concurrent edits and source originals, and apply changes only within the requested artifact scope. Full drafting and rewriting are supported when requested.
Use `nonfiction-manuscript-editor` for thesis and chapter architecture, `fact-checking-editor` for verification, `citation-integrity-checker` for citations, and `line-copy-editor` for the later copy pass.
Return exactly these sections: `Draft`, `Source And Claim Notes`, `Editorial Decisions`, `Coverage And Checks`, `Open Queries`, `Files Changed`, `Handoffs`.
"

commands.command: /bin/bash -lc "sed -n '1,260p' .agents/skills/text-composition/artifacts/nonfiction-drafting-kit.md && for f in inputs/refrain.md inputs/witnesses.md inputs/copy.md inputs/proof.md inputs/index-source.md inputs/edition-source.md; do printf '\\n%s\\n' \""'$f"; sed -n '"'1,220p' \""'$f"; done && file inputs/book.epub && unzip -l inputs/book.epub | sed -n '"'1,100p'"

/bin/bash -lc "sed -n '1,320p' .agents/skills/text-composition/references/artifacts/nonfiction-drafting-kit.md && for f in inputs/refrain.md inputs/witnesses.md inputs/copy.md inputs/proof.md inputs/index-source.md inputs/edition-source.md; do printf '\\n%s\\n' \""'$f"; sed -n '"'1,220p' \""'$f"; done && file inputs/book.epub && unzip -l inputs/book.epub | sed -n '"'1,100p'"

/bin/bash -lc "for f in mimetype META-INF/container.xml EPUB/package.opf EPUB/nav.xhtml EPUB/chapter.xhtml; do printf '\\ninputs/book.epub:%s\\n' \""'$f"; unzip -p inputs/book.epub "$f"; done && git status --short && find outputs -maxdepth 2 -type f -print 2>/dev/null'
/bin/bash -lc 'find .agents/skills -maxdepth 2 -name SKILL.md -print | sort && find outputs -maxdepth 2 -type f -print 2>/dev/null || true'

/bin/bash -lc "draft_text='What This Library Survey Tells Us—and What It Does Not

A short survey at the neighborhood library offers a useful snapshot, provided its boundaries remain clear. Thirty people responded, and 18 of them—60 percent—said they use the library weekly. Among the people who chose to answer that day, regular library use was common.

That finding can help the library understand the experience of visitors who were present at its entrance on one Saturday. It may justify follow-up questions about services for frequent users, such as borrowing, programs, computers, or study space. It does not, however, establish how often all neighborhood residents use the library.

The recruitment method matters. Because everyone was approached at the library entrance, the survey was more likely to reach people already visiting the library than people who seldom visit or do not visit. The single-Saturday timing also leaves open whether the respondents differed from visitors on other days or at other times. These are limits on who the result represents, not evidence that the 18 reports were inaccurate.

There is also no citywide comparison. We therefore cannot say whether weekly use in this group is higher, lower, or similar to use elsewhere in the city. Nor can the survey identify why respondents use the library, because no interviews or additional studies were included.

The practical conclusion is modest but valuable: 18 of 30 surveyed entrance visitors reported weekly use. To learn about the wider neighborhood or city, future surveying would need to reach residents beyond the entrance and compare results across places and times.'; printf '%s\\n' \""'$draft_text" | wc -w'

disposition: Content failure: inferred that the underlying survey did not ask a question from absence of details in the packet. Added an explicit missing-packet-evidence rule and reran.
